reachable: Yes, at the scored position and with gradient. (1) SCORING: cups_probe.stream_coded_toks re-derives the coding per arm from each arm's own command strings, so the coded token is the model's input at every command position of a scored window including the read; the read token is bit-identical across arms (measured 0.0 max abs diff on a synthetic role swap, /tmp/rev26/check11.py) while mv tokens differ by 5.14. (2) The arch's transported content reaches the prediction: tr_reads -> g_tr * tr_read(tr_reads) is added to pred_cmd at command positions. (3) At the scored read the memory WRITE is gated off (active = valid_obs & valid_cmd, false there) but the READ is not, and reads[i] is appended before the write, so the transported content is available exactly where it is scored. (4) GRADIENT: tr_path_dst is a (64,176) matrix and the r18 optim's Muon key group picks it up alongside tr_path (verified: muon params include tr_path_dst.weight, no parameter is left out of an optimizer, /tmp/rev26/check8.py). Its gradient is exactly 0 at step 0 because tr_read is zero-init, then becomes nonzero as tr_read grows; a 60-step real-data run gives ||tr_path_dst - tr_path|| = 0.50 with tr_read norm 3.66 (/tmp/rev26/check9.py). That bootstrapping bottleneck is inherited from r18/r22, not introduced here. (5) Training data supplies the mechanism's signal: every one of the 2560 training sequences contains mv steps (2-13 per sequence). (6) The mechanism is structurally capable, not just nominally present: with hand-set addressing weights the dual-key memory carries content across A->B->C and returns it at a later read with cosine 1.0000 and norm preserved, while the parent's single-address memory returns exactly the zero vector at the destination (/tmp/rev26/check6.py). That also confirms the hypothesis's claim about both parents being structurally incapable of transport.
solves_outside_model: No. The stream parses each command string in isolation and writes only functions of that string plus that command's own 768-d embedding: _compact(cmd) takes one string; code_cmds loops rows independently; the count-sketch is a fixed permutation+sign gather of the single row. No observation, no other step, no cross-step state, no cached chain resolution (the module-level cache is keyed by the command string and returns a pure function of it). Verified by execution: prefix-causal at every cut (coding cmds[:k+1] equals the first k+1 rows of coding the whole list, all k), idempotent, and the read token identical between the native and role-swapped chains. The arch touches no strings at all. Nothing resembling the retracted +0.9026 shape: the model is handed two separable operands per command and a memory that CAN move a value between two addresses, but composing hops is left entirely to learned parameters (a_read, a_write, the mutation gate, the transition operator, the zero-init readout) -- and at init tr_path_dst == tr_path, so the model starts at exactly the parent function (max |pred diff| vs r22 = 0.0, and no inherited parameter differs, /tmp/rev26/check5.py). One nuance the parent should be aware of rather than a violation: the coding makes a bounded backward trace cheaper to represent, but the eligible slice is depth 3-4 and DEPTH_MIN sits above the bounded-trace caps (1,2), so a trace short enough to be a shortcut does not solve a scored window; the analytic band is measured and reported anyway.
summary:
The code does what the hypothesis says. Every load-bearing structural claim checked out by execution, not reading.

Verified true: (a) the parent r22 and partner r18 archs both address the transition memory with ONE projection used as read and write key, so they cannot transport content across a move -- confirmed by rigging the parent to a 2-hop chain and getting the exact zero vector at the destination; (b) the candidate's step equations match the hypothesis line for line (s_pre at the read address, v = (1-g)obs + g*transition(s_pre), delta-rule write at the WRITE address correcting against d_pre, read appended before the write); (c) tr_path_dst is copied from tr_path at init and the module is bit-identical to r22 at init (max |pred diff| 0.0, no inherited parameter perturbed); (d) with hand-set weights the dual-key memory transports A->B->C and returns the source content at the read with cosine 1.0000; (e) the collate is byte-for-byte the baseline layout except the command half -- types, key_pad, tgt, cmd_mask and the observation tokens are equal to M.collate's; (f) the parser behaves exactly as described on real strings and on the edge forms it names (cat/ls take src as dst; '>' and '>>' set an explicit dst; flags -f skipped); (g) the coding is prefix-causal, idempotent and read-token-identical across arms.

MEASURED numbers the author could not have run through the harness: the two he could compute in a jail with numpy+hashlib both reproduce. The claim that the identity codes of backup.job.5 and backup.job.6 have inner product -0.14 in block-width units reproduces at exactly -0.1375, and self-inner-product is 1.0; random path pairs have |ip| std 0.0796. The sketch distortion claim (mean |cos err| 0.030, max 0.074 on 30 correlated Gaussian pairs) reproduces at 0.024/0.105 with my own correlated construction -- same order, no misrepresentation -- and I went further and measured it on 3000 pairs of REAL standardized command embeddings: mean 0.034, p95 0.088, max 0.216. So his declared risk #2 ('real embeddings are correlated and the true distortion could be worse') is now measured and is only marginally worse than his Gaussian estimate.

The only figure that is wrong is the one he explicitly flagged as a guess (see divergences): the path-set block carries 95.3 not ~58 energy, and shared-path cosine is 0.599 not 0.4-0.55. The consequence runs in the safe direction -- path_thresh 0.32 mines 96.2% of shared-path pairs at a 2.3% false-positive rate, versus the parent's 80.2% / 13.6% at 0.60 -- so the partner's head contribution is retained and sharpened, not lost.

WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK. (1) Risk #1, the author's own headline risk: whether the 176-d cmd_proj bottleneck learns separable source and destination subspaces at the real step budget. My 60-step CPU run shows the split beginning (||dst-src|| 0.50) but the addresses are still 0.988 cosine apart from each other, which is what you would expect that early and says nothing about the full budget. If it does not separate, the arch falls back to the parent function, which is where it starts -- a null, not a corruption. (2) Address crosstalk: key_d is 64 and a window exposes many distinct paths, so the near-orthogonal 160-d codes are compressed into a 64-d key space; interference and capacity are neither analysed by the author nor measured by me. He discusses erasure (risk #4) but not this. (3) Whether comp_ca actually moves. The parent sits at +0.0000 and the noise floor is 0.0227 on a three-seed draw. (4) Speed (his risk #5): my CPU loop ran ~0.22 s/step at bs=16; that does not extrapolate to the GPU lane.

ONE INSTRUMENT CAVEAT FOR THE PARENT, not a defect of this candidate: evolve/cdh_probe.py builds its tokens straight from s['z_cmd'] and has no code_cmds hook at all, so the cd-pack number printed beside this candidate's score is measured with UNCODED command tokens on a net trained on coded ones -- off-distribution and not comparable to a baseline-stream genome's cdh reading. cdh is never scored, so selection is unaffected, but the reported figure should not be read as this genome's routing capability. This affects any stream that codes command tokens, so it is a repo gap worth a task rather than a mark against slot26.

divergences.claim: Risk-3 geometry estimate: 'from the block energies (identity 160+160, path-set ~58, directories ~14 each, verb ~12, flags 8, sketch 256) a pair sharing one path in one role retains roughly 0.4-0.55 cosine and an unrelated pair in a shared directory roughly 0.2, so I set path_thresh to 0.32.'
divergences.what_the_code_does: Measured on 300 real training sequences (standardized cache data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd/emb-seq-train.pt) after code_cmds: id_src 157.3, id_dst 157.3, pset 95.3 (not ~58), dir 14.2 each, verb 11.8, flags 8.0, sketch 249.6. The pset figure is off because the many src==dst commands (every cat/ls read) put 2*code in that block, quadrupling per-coordinate energy instead of doubling it. Consequently shared-path cosine is HIGHER than estimated: mean 0.599, median 0.592, p05 0.346 (vs claimed 0.4-0.55); unrelated same-directory is mean 0.255, median 0.229 (vs claimed ~0.2).
divergences.evidence: /tmp/rev26/check3.py and /tmp/rev26/check10.py. At path_thresh=0.32: 96.2% of shared-path pairs mined, 21.3% of same-directory unrelated pairs, 1.0% of fully unrelated pairs -> 2.3% overall false-positive rate. The parent's raw-embedding mining at 0.60 gives 80.2% recall and 13.6% false positives (/tmp/rev26/check4.py). So the threshold the author guessed is not merely safe, it strictly improves the head's mining; the aux does not silently return 0.0. The author explicitly labelled this number 'an estimate, not a measurement -- I could not run the harness', so the miss is disclosed, not asserted.
